clue.text: Slag off lad backing start of this greater openness

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong tells us to jumble the word slag
backing means the word for lad is read from back to front

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son

indicators.note: start of picks out the opening letter of the word this

explanation.surface: Someone insults a boy before praising the new transparency of a regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SLAG into GLAS; 'backing' turns SON into NOS; T comes from 'start of this'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet policy of the 1980s brought more political transparency, the literal sense of the Russian word.

clue.text: Muddled situation involving men in one of the services

indicators.note: involving means one word wraps round and contains the other

parts.note: Mass is a church service
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Chaos in the armed forces when the troops get caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the services' suggests the army or navy, and OR (other ranks) supports that, but the service here is the Mass of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or swamp, and figuratively a confused state that is hard to escape.

clue.text: Selfishly secure return of speaker's gift

indicators.note: return of means the letters of the gift word come back in reverse order

parts.note: the gift of the gab is a talent for fluent talk

explanation.surface: Someone greedily grabs back the present a lecturer was given.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to grab it for yourself before anyone else can claim it.

clue.text: Relative given cut by distinguished writer from East

parts.note: distinguished means eminent, great

indicators.note: read from east to west in an across clue, that is right to left, so the writer is backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A family member is snubbed by a famous Eastern author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from East' turns PEN into NEP; the pieces are then strung together in the answer's order rather than the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: The grandson of your brother or sister is a family member one generation below a nephew.

clue.text: New arrangement for tall riders facing bleak prospects

indicators.note: a new arrangement says the letters of the following words are reordered

explanation.surface: Lanky jockeys are rearranged on their mounts, with poor chances of winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New arrangement for' rearranges TALL RIDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally born under unlucky stars, so doomed or likely to fail.

clue.text: Disallow cipher, following check

indicators.note: following places the cipher after the word for check

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
a cipher is a zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An official blocks a secret code after inspecting it.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto is to forbid or reject a proposal by authority.

clue.text: Yob in train, not in horse-drawn carriage

indicators.note: in places the yob inside what remains of the train
not means the following little word is removed from the word train

parts.note: taken as written
an oik is a British slang word for a lout

explanation.surface: A thug on the railway is not on a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' leaves TRA from the train; 'oik' is British slang for an uncouth lout, and the first 'in' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian vehicle drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Enduring a posh girl's confining quarters

indicators.note: confining means the girl's word wraps round the quarters

parts.note: gel is an upper-class pronunciation of girl; the possessive gives the S
E and S are two compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: A society girl's room keeps her going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gel' mocks the way upper-class Britons say girl; its possessive S stays after the quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ageless lasts without seeming to grow old, so it is enduring.

clue.text: Flying craft — what one needs to succeed, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: to succeed to a title one must be the heir, holding heirship

explanation.surface: A balloon-like vessel is what you need for success, people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means inherit, not do well.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered, steerable lighter-than-air vessel such as a zeppelin.

clue.text: Up-to-date info from City match?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: The news from a big-city game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a full international game of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest is the most recent news, as in what's the latest.

clue.text: Endlessly lively venture

indicators.note: endlessly removes an end letter, here the front one, of the word for lively

parts.note: brisk means lively and quick

explanation.surface: A bold undertaking carried out with constant energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes B off BRISK.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture is to dare or chance something, which is to take a gamble.

clue.text: It enrages one reassembling equipment for blockade

indicators.note: reassembling means putting the letters together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man is furious at having to put kit back together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reassembling' rearranges ITENRAGES plus I from 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of heavy guns and supplies taken along to besiege a town.

clue.text: Sturdy press employee stumbling in at last

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper

indicators.note: stumbling suggests the letters of the following words lurch out of order

explanation.surface: A newspaper worker finally staggers in, solid on his feet at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' rearranges IN AT LAST to give STANTIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Substantial means solidly built and strong.

clue.text: Operatic princess's days in island area

indicators.note: in places the days inside the island and area

explanation.surface: A royal singer's days are spent on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the title role of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera named after her.

clue.text: Redcap in old film freed from obligation

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: in places the military policeman inside the other letters

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film
a redcap is a British military policeman, MP

explanation.surface: A soldier in a vintage movie is released from his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the cap colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means excused from a duty or rule.

clue.text: Study bird, initially one with unknown name

indicators.note: initially puts the letter for one at the very start

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a den is a private study
a tit is a small bird
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher studies, first alone, then with an unidentified companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' places I at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Who you are, as given by your name, is your identity.

clue.text: Ugly dwarf eatin' revoltin'ly, by the sound of it!

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals that the word is judged by its pronunciation

parts.note: gobbling, with the dropped g, is eating greedily and revoltingly

explanation.surface: A rough-spoken comment on a dwarf who eats disgustingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g's set up gobblin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a small, grotesque, mischievous creature in folklore.

clue.text: Sharp-cornered or ring-shaped, not new but good

indicators.note: not new but good says swap the letter for new with the letter for good

parts.note: annular means ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A shape described as either angular or round, but good rather than new.
explanation.walkthrough: N for new is replaced by G for good.
explanation.definitionFit: Having sharp angles or corners.

clue.text: What enables one to see and hear horseman land

indicators.note: hear signals a word that is the same when said but spelt differently

parts.note: a knight is a mounted warrior
to light is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: A rider sees and hears a cavalryman coming down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is a verb: to light on something is to alight there.
explanation.definitionFit: A dim lamp left on after dark lets people find their way.

clue.text: Organised drive to defame cameraman: GP is involved

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A doctor is mixed up in a photographer's plan to ruin someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges CAMERAMAN GP IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A coordinated effort to damage someone's reputation with damaging claims.

clue.text: Sign rejected in Benedictine monasteries

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A symbol turned away by Benedictine religious houses.
explanation.walkthrough: NEMO hides in 'BenedictiNE MOnasteries'; 'rejected' turns it back and 'in' signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Fulfil challenge ultimately, visiting record office, right away

indicators.note: visiting means one piece goes into the other
away means the right letter is taken out of the record office

parts.note: an archive is a place where records are kept

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of challenge

explanation.surface: Meet the challenge in the end by going to the records office, right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R from ARCHIVE to leave ACHIVE; 'ultimately' supplies E, which 'visiting' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something is to accomplish or fulfil it.

clue.text: Woodworker's supporter observed taking addictive drug

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see, observed
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A carpenter's friend was seen using drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame on which a carpenter rests wood for sawing.

clue.text: Laborious task regularly undertaken in coffee shop?

definitions.text: Laborious task regularly undertaken in coffee shop?

parts.words: Laborious task regularly undertaken in coffee shop?
parts.note: the everyday dull work routine, playfully pictured as the coffee beans ground each day in a café

explanation.surface: Grinding coffee every day at the café.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A common idiom for the tedious routine of one's working life.

clue.text: Write rubbish: hard line about athletic contest

parts.note: to pen is to write
tat is cheap rubbish
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A writer dismisses rubbish about a demanding sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-event competition in modern athletics and the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Game left over at end of table

parts.note: across means over, on the other side

indicators.note: at end of picks out the final letter of the word table

explanation.surface: A game is abandoned at the end of a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Ludicrous, showing anger about brother or sister

indicators.note: about means the word for anger surrounds the sibling

parts.note: to rile is to anger
a sib is a sibling

explanation.surface: Absurd displays of temper over a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable, ridiculous.

clue.text: In Westminster area, worry about husband's language

indicators.note: in places the inner word inside the postcode

parts.note: SW1 is Westminster's London postcode

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes round the husband

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or worry
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: In the Westminster district, a wife frets about her husband's way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postcode for Westminster, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu tongue widely spoken in East Africa.

clue.text: Incautious Republican brought down in part of airport

indicators.note: brought down means the letter is moved lower, here further down the word in a down clue

parts.note: a runway is where planes take off and land

explanation.surface: A careless politician is taken down on the airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought down' moves R from the top of RUNWAY to lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwary means not on one's guard.

clue.text: Measure Society darling overturned

indicators.note: overturned means the darling word is flipped upside down in a down clue

parts.note: a pet is a darling

explanation.surface: A society favourite is knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measure taken to achieve something.
